page: Amazon Web Services m6a.xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It features an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server is configured with 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores, supporting hyper-threading with 2 threads per core. It includes 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25 percent. However, multi-core performance is average, and memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with both small-block and large-block read and write operations scoring in the bottom 25 percent. Computational tasks such as single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench text processing perform at average levels, while multi-threaded decompression, software compilation, and database operations show weaker relative performance.

The qualitative cost profile of the m6a.xlarge reflects a balanced general-purpose resource density, offering dedicated CPU allocation at a lower entry tier. Given the weak memory bandwidth and database operation benchmarks, this instance is less suited for high-throughput databases or memory-intensive applications. It is best utilized for general-purpose workloads, light web serving, single-threaded processing tasks, and basic development environments where single-core CPU performance is prioritized over high memory throughput.
